text:
Morgan Rielly came back into the lineup against Chicago on Nov. 17 (Sportsnet and NHL.com both flagged the return) and walked into a hard week in Toronto. Daily Faceoff Toronto reported that he and Jack Roslovic had been taking "value from conversations with Rory McIlroy's sports psychologist amid 8-game losing streak."

His own season is an odd one: 12 points in 20 games, every one an assist. That scoring rate, 1.88 points per 60, sits above the top of our range for him, so the assists have run a little hot. The goals have gone the other way. He has 0 on 1.6 expected goals (the quality of his chances), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among defensemen last season for chances from the home-plate area in front of the net. A defenseman who gets there usually scores now and then.

The defensive side is the long-running worry. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more with him on last season (bottom 5% of defensemen), and the Leafs get 47.4% of the 5v5 expected goals with him this year. Our range for his season is 30 to 47 points.
